```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(dbplyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
PSTAT132db <- dbConnect(
  RSQLite::SQLite(),
  "PSTAT132-db.sqlite"
)
```

Getting the first 10 customers- retrieving customer_id, name, and region for the first 10 customers
```{r}
first10 <- dbGetQuery(PSTAT132db, "
SELECT customer_id, name, region
FROM customers
LIMIT 10;
")
first10
```

customer_id, name, and region of customers who spent more than 150$ (total_spend > 150)
Using dbGetQuery() and using dbplyr() pipes

Using dbGetQuery()
```{r}
high_spenders <- dbGetQuery(PSTAT132db, "
                            SELECT customer_id, name, region
                            FROM customers
                            WHERE total_spend > 150;
                            ")
high_spenders
```

Using dplyr pipes:
```{r}
high_spenders_pipe <- tbl(PSTAT132db, "customers") %>% 
  filter(total_spend > 150) %>% 
  select(customer_id, name, region) %>% 
  #at this point, dbplyr generally builds a query that the database can execute, but you have only described what data you want, and haven't collected the results into a regular R data frame 
  #collect tells the database to run the query and send the matching results into R 
  collect() #this executes the query and brings the resulting rows into R 

high_spenders_pipe
```

Performing a case-insensitive search and saving the result as 'widget_products' for products containing 'widget' 
Using SQL 
```{r}
widget_products <- dbGetQuery(PSTAT132db, "
                              SELECT *
                              FROM products
                              WHERE product_name LIKE '%widget%' COLLATE NOCASE;
                              ")

widget_products
```

Writing the dbplyr equivalent and using show_query
```{r}
widget_products_pipe <- tbl(PSTAT132db, "products") %>% 
  filter(sql("product_name LIKE '%widget%' COLLATE NOCASE"))

show_query(widget_products_pipe)

#collect() takes the query results from the database and brings them into r as a regular data frame or tibble 
widget_products <- collect(widget_products_pipe)
#collect(table_or_query), but most commonly, you leave it at the end of a pipe
```
